title: Adopter success pockets and quickcheck runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact runbook for early adopters and internal engineers who onboard teams to the Redwood SDKs. It is intentionally short, pragmatic, and oriented around the first 60 minutes and first 1,000 requests. Use it in customer-facing labs, AE/SE handoffs, and internal ramps.

High-level goals:
- Get a product/engineer from API key -> sample app running in 20 minutes
- Detect the 5 most common failure modes in the first day and provide quick mitigations
- Ensure telemetry and cost guardrails are enabled before any sustained traffic
- Provide a reproducible rollback and cutover checklist for experiments and feature flags

Quickcheck checklist (first 20 minutes):
1) Credentials and network
   - Confirm API key is created and scoped to the right org/project (ask: which project?).
   - Validate network egress: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health (should return 200).
   - If private deployment: ensure VPC peering and KMS access included.
2) Minimal sample run
   - Clone minimal sample (link in linked_artifacts).
   - Run: node example/hello-redwood.js or python hello.py. Expect a short generation under 3s.
   - If timing out: increase request timeout to 30s and capture logs.
3) Telemetry and cost safe-guards
   - Turn on dev-level telemetry: set SDK_ENV=dev and verify token-level telemetry shows up in Console > Routes > last 24h.
   - Configure per-route rate limits (soft limit 50rps) and a daily quota.
   - Add quota alert to Slack channel using alert hook.
4) Prompt / output sanity tests
   - Send 10 deterministic prompts (seeded) and snapshot outputs. Compare token length ranges to model profile.
   - If hallucination risk: include scoring prompt for confidence or call reranker flow.

Common failure modes and quick remedies:
- 401 / invalid key: check key rotation policy and that the key isn’t a limited-scope service token. Regenerate and re-run quick test.
- High variance latency: check model choice (base vs. long-context), confirm model pinned correctly in request, inspect region mismatch (client in us-west vs. model hosted in europe-west). Swap to same-region model variant to test.
- Unexpected high token cost: verify batch size / sampling params, check loop that may be re-sending prompt (idempotency tokens), enable token-level cost logging; set soft quota.
- Missing telemetry: agent might be running older SDK. Perform `npm ls @redwood/sdk` or `pip show redwood-sdk` and upgrade to newest patch.
- Private deployment KMS failures: inspect IAM roles attached to instance & KMS key policy. Temporary workaround: use a short-lived service token from the control plane.

Three short lab scenarios (15–40 minutes each) to validate production readiness:
1) Tiny prototyping loop (15m)
   - Goal: run a semantic-search demo using embeddings and a single route.
   - Checks: embedding length, storage wiring, retries on 429.
2) Rate-burst resilience (30m)
   - Goal: simulate a burst of 300 concurrent short requests to a single route.
   - Checks: autoscaling behavior, fallback policy to cheaper-variant, circuit-breaker activation and alert firing.
3) Canary roll and rollback (40m)
   - Goal: deploy a canary model variant to 5% traffic, observe QPS/latency/cost, then rollback on failure.
   - Checks: feature-flag toggles, telemetry enrichments, traffic split mechanics, cleanup steps.

Telemetry quick wins and minimal required signals:
- Required signals (should be visible in first 24h): per-route token consumption, p50/p95 latency, error-type histogram (4xx, 5xx, timeouts), model-variant identifier.
- Helpful signals: prompt fingerprinting (hash), repetition rate per-user, latency-by-sequence-length.
- Cheap probes to add to code immediately: add SDK hook to tag requests with `test_run_id` and a local counter; expose these in Console logs for trace correlation.

Rollback and emergency cutover checklist:
- Immediately flip route to a stable model variant (document the exact variant name).
- Disable all autoscale burst policies for the route to prevent noisy neighbor spike.
- Revoke the suspect key and issue a replacement if a token compromise is suspected.
- If private control plane: open ticket with infra-team and gather kube/pod logs (pod: redwood-router-*)
- Communicate to customer: one-sentence status + ETA for next update, include a link to telemetry dashboard.

Safety and guardrails to enable by default in demo accounts:
- Soft quota at 2500 tokens/day for trial tenants; hard block at 25k tokens/day unless explicitly raised.
- Default model for sample apps should be the cost-balanced variant (e.g., rwd-small-v1) not the largest.
- All sample prompts in repo must include a visible ‘do_not_send_to_prod’ tag to avoid accidental reuse.

Developer handoff notes for AE/SEs:
- Share the `quickcheck` script in samples that runs the 10 deterministic prompts and posts results to Slack.
- Keep a one-page crib: how to run the canary rollback (3 commands), how to find the trace in Console (route + test_run_id).
- When escalating: include the sample prompt, request id/timestamp, SDK version, and region.

Open items / TODOs:
- Add a small GUI widget in the onboarding flow that offers to enable telemetry + set a soft quota (UX ticket).
- Create a short recorded demo (3–4 minutes) that runs through the Quickcheck checklist end-to-end.
- Flesh out a private-deployment appendix with exact KMS role examples and terraform templates.

Notes to self / scratchpad (things I scribbled while testing):
- Diego: the Node sample times out intermittently on our lab cluster; maybe bump default timeout in examples to 20s.
- Priya: confirm the canary traffic split API respects feature flags in dedicated and hosted.
- Consider small `redwood quickcheck` CLI that runs the 4 quick probes and returns a pass/fail code for automation.

Minimal sample commands (copyable):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small-v1","input":"hello"}'
- node examples/diagnostic.js --test-run-id=qrk-20241118
- REDWOOD_ENV=dev python3 examples/quickcheck.py --profile=canary

If you run this in a customer session, keep it tight. Start from credentials -> minimal sample -> telemetry -> 1 lab. If everything is green, a 30 minute follow-up lab can exercise canary rollouts and scaling.

End of runbook.
summary: Compact draft runbook for early adopter SDK onboarding: quickchecks, failure modes, 3 labs, telemetry and rollback checklist. For eng-devexp / AE handoffs.
